read.thesis: Marriott Q3 2026 RevPAR +6.5% and full-year RevPAR guide raised to 4.5-5% from 1.5-2.5%, but supply signals are soft: global new-build starts down 24% and Q4 EMEA RevPAR expected to decline.

capex.peers_comment: Capuano said it is a competitive environment, with key money the weapon of choice against competitors in conversions.
capex.quote: Whether we like it or not, key money seems to be the weapon of choice against that competitive landscape.

triggers.label: Global new-build starts down 24%
triggers.quote: Globally, which I think was the second part of your question, year to date through the first three quarters of the year, new build construction starts were down about 24%.

triggers.label: FY26 RevPAR guide raised to 4.5-5%
triggers.quote: We now expect 4.5%-5% global RevPAR growth.

triggers.label: U.S. new-build starts up 20% YTD
triggers.quote: Through the first three quarters this year, new build construction starts are up 20% year over year.

triggers.label: Key money deal premium 65% to 75%
triggers.quote: Year to date through the first three quarters this year, those deals where we deployed key money had an average premium per room of about 75%.

guidance.quote: We now expect 4.5%-5% global RevPAR growth.
leads to expected full-year adjusted diluted EPS growth of 20%-21%.
we are raising our gross fee guidance to an increase of around 13%
our full-year 2026 capital returns to shareholders are now expected to be at least $4.8 billion.
Investment spending is still expected to be $1.25 billion-$1.35 billion
Global RevPAR in the fourth quarter is anticipated to increase 4.5%-5%.
Fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase 12%-14%.
Our preliminary view is that the 2027 year-over-year global RevPAR growth could be 3.5%-4.5%.
we still expect net rooms growth towards the low end of our prior 4.5%-5% range

prior_guidance_check.quote: This is well above the 1.5%-2.5% growth range we initially forecast on our year-end 2025 earnings call
Our outlook for full-year 2026 key money and total investment spending has not changed.

red_flags.label: Owner friction over incentive fees
red_flags.quote: I'd love to just get your updated thoughts on the owner relation topic.

red_flags.label: Net rooms growth guided to low end
red_flags.quote: we still expect net rooms growth towards the low end of our prior 4.5%-5% range

evasions.quote: sometimes I get the sense there is an expectation of a big reveal.
I am not quite ready to really give you much more of a peek into 2027
